source: rig --help, recursive (read-only); curated fields hand-written from --help, installed docs and our runs · copied from brains/openrig/rig-commands.json

effects.changes state: writes a record or sends something

commands.openrig_says: Show daemon logs
commands.plain: Shows the background service's recent log.
commands.when_to_use: When a command fails and the error is unclear.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Start the daemon
commands.plain: Starts the OpenRig background service that runs every team on this machine.
commands.when_to_use: After a reboot or a `rig daemon stop`, when `rig daemon status` says it is down.
commands.when_not: Never from inside a Claude session: every seat would inherit that session's environment (the d09-crew README trap). Use `rig start` if you also want rigs restored.
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)
commands.example: rig daemon stop && rig daemon start   # then open http://127.0.0.1:7433

commands.openrig_says: Show daemon status
commands.plain: Says whether the background service is running.
commands.when_to_use: First check when anything looks broken.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Stop the daemon (10s shutdown budget; 12s process wait; incomplete drain exits nonzero)
commands.plain: Stops the background service. Running agents keep their tmux sessions but nothing coordinates them.
commands.when_to_use: Before an upgrade, or to restart a misbehaving daemon.
commands.when_not: Not from a Claude session, and not while a team is mid-job unless you mean to pause everything.
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)

commands.openrig_says: Destroy OpenRig local state for recovery
commands.plain: Wipes OpenRig's local state for recovery.
commands.when_to_use: Last resort, with support guidance.
commands.when_not: Almost never. It loses teams, queue and history.
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)

commands.openrig_says: Check installation, provider authentication, writable paths, port/daemon and conditional cmux control
commands.plain: Checks the install: dependencies, folders, port, daemon.
commands.when_to_use: First step when OpenRig won't work.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Check system readiness for OpenRig
commands.plain: Checks the machine is ready for OpenRig.
commands.when_to_use: Before first use on a machine.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: The whole four-block provider read model (accounts, bindings, signals)
commands.plain: Shows accounts, which agent uses which, and usage signals seen on this machine.
commands.when_to_use: Checking how much allowance is left (on our M4 it reports "unknown"; the M2 shows weekly %).
commands.when_not: Add --all-hosts for every machine in the fleet.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Prepare the machine for OpenRig
commands.plain: Prepares the machine for OpenRig: writes into ~/.claude, ~/.agents, ~/.codex, ~/.tmux.conf.
commands.when_to_use: First install on a machine, by David.
commands.when_not: Never on a machine you don't mean to change; never from a Claude session.
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)

commands.openrig_says: Start the daemon, verify kernel, and restore rigs that were last running
commands.plain: Starts the background service, checks the built-in "kernel" helpers, and brings back the teams that were running.
commands.when_to_use: After a reboot, to get everything back in one go (`--last` for no prompts).
commands.when_not: Not from a Claude session (it starts the daemon).
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)

commands.openrig_says: Install a .rigbundle or GitHub folder link (bootstrap from bundle)
commands.plain: Installs a packaged team (a bundle, e.g. Mike's Workshop) and launches it.
commands.when_to_use: Trying a published rig from openrig.dev/rigs (run with `--plan` first).
commands.when_not: Workshop ships with permission prompts off; read it first.
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)

commands.openrig_says: Install a pack; --git discovers a pack in a Git repository and retains its update relationship
commands.plain: Adds a context pack to the library, e.g. from git.
commands.when_to_use: Installing Mike's openrig-world pack.
commands.when_not: Writes to OpenRig home; auto mode may refuse it.
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)

commands.openrig_says: List all context packs in the library
commands.plain: Lists context packs (bundles of instructions agents can load).
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: List library rigs, agents, and managed apps
commands.plain: Lists rig and agent specs in the library.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Create a new mission with SPEC.md and mission.yaml (mints a stable dot-ID into frontmatter)
commands.plain: Creates a mission record (a body of work) in OpenRig's workspace.
commands.when_to_use: Start of a multi-step job, so tags and Refocus have something to point at.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session
commands.example: rig scope mission create d09 --intent "Eight features across eight repos, one at a time"

commands.openrig_says: List missions (top-level folders with SPEC.md or a legacy README.md)
commands.plain: Lists mission records.
commands.when_to_use: Before creating one, to avoid duplicates.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Create a new slice with SPEC.md, slice.yaml, PROGRESS.md, PROOF.md, and proof/. Conventions SSOT: docs/reference/sdlc-conventions.md (installed: $OPENRIG_HOME/reference/sdlc-conventions.md).
commands.plain: Creates one job (slice) inside a mission, with its goal line.
commands.when_to_use: One per job in a mission.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session
commands.example: rig scope slice create d09 appystack-light-theme --intent "AppyStack template uses the AppyDave light theme"

commands.openrig_says: Manually run the guided compaction sequence (prep → /compact → restore → audit) for one Claude seat
commands.plain: Runs a guided compaction for one Claude agent: prep, /compact, restore, audit.
commands.when_to_use: An agent near its context limit that should keep going.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Hand a seat to a successor: create -> deliver context -> verify continuity -> rebind
commands.plain: Hands a seat to a new agent: create, pass context, check, rebind.
commands.when_to_use: An agent near its context limit, or a planned change of agent.
commands.when_not: Use `--dry-run` first.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Launch a deliberate fresh occupant for exactly one existing seat
commands.plain: Puts a fresh agent into an existing seat (no old conversation).
commands.when_to_use: Daily fresh start of a permanent seat (`--fresh --stop`).
commands.when_not: It does not resume the old conversation; use `rig up --existing` for that.
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)
commands.example: rig seat launch dev-impl@my-rig --fresh --reason "deliberate blank restart"

commands.openrig_says: Show read-only seat handover observability status
commands.plain: Shows a seat's handover state.
commands.when_to_use: Before or after a handover.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.plain: Stops one agent (closes its terminal) and leaves its seat defined.
commands.when_to_use: One stuck or finished agent.
commands.when_not: Ends its work in progress; check with `rig capture` first.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Submit and inspect startup orientation proof
commands.plain: Lets an agent prove it read its start instructions.
commands.where_to_run: inside a seat (reads OPENRIG_SESSION_NAME); from outside pass --source

commands.openrig_says: Show current managed identity in an OpenRig topology

commands.when_not: Outside a seat it has nothing to report.

commands.openrig_says: Archive a rig (soft + reversible: hides it from the default view, retains all data). NOT a delete; reverse with 'rig unarchive'.
commands.plain: Hides a team from the default list, keeping all its data.

commands.when_not: It is not a delete; `rig unarchive` reverses it.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.plain: Makes a one-agent team without writing a rig.yaml.

commands.when_not: For anything permanent write a rig.yaml so it can be reviewed and relaunched.
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)

commands.openrig_says: Tear down a rig
commands.plain: Stops a whole team: saves each agent's conversation id and a snapshot, then closes their terminals. The team stays defined.

commands.when_not: Not while agents are mid-job unless you mean to stop them; worktrees and branches stay.
commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Launch or relaunch a node in a running rig
commands.plain: Launches or relaunches one agent in a running team.

commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)

commands.plain: Lists teams (rigs), or with `--nodes` every agent in them, with running/idle state.

commands.openrig_says: Show rig status

commands.openrig_says: Launch a rig or managed app from a spec, library entry, or bundle
commands.plain: Starts a team from its rig.yaml, or brings a stopped team back by name (`--existing`), optionally with fresh agents (`--fresh <seat>`).
commands.when_to_use: To launch a team; or with `--existing` to wake a stopped one with its conversations.
commands.when_not: Claude Code's auto mode may refuse it ("Create Unsafe Agents"); run it yourself. `partially_restored` exits 1 even when a fresh start worked: check `rig ps`, not the exit code.
commands.where_to_run: plain terminal (never a Claude session)
commands.example: rig up /Users/davidcruwys/dev/ad/brains/openrig/rigs/d09-crew/rig.yaml   |   rig up openrig-watch --existing --fresh watch.keeper --yes

commands.plain: Shows explained health findings for a seat, team or the machine.

commands.where_to_run: anywhere: plain terminal or a Claude session

commands.openrig_says: Register a watchdog; queue block --wake-watchdog attaches its job id. Context transcripts measured 113K–153K tokens/MB. The margin is the protection because prompt-bound consumers act only at turn boundaries

commands.openrig_says: Park a qitem as HELD with a continuation and wake. Requires --on <blocker>. Choose --wake-watchdog, --wake-after, or a live blocker qitem for the wake.
commands.plain: Puts a work item aside on purpose, with a timer or blocker that will wake its owner later.

commands.when_not: The timer only nudges a running agent; it does not start a stopped one.

commands.example: rig queue block <task> --on external:release-pr --wake-after 1h --continuation "check the PR; re-arm"

commands.openrig_says: Create a new qitem

commands.openrig_says: Append a note and/or mutate qitem state. A note without --state never changes row state. state=done REQUIRES --closure-reason (one of: handed_off_to, blocked_on, denied, canceled, no-follow-on, escalation). Closure ≠ acceptance: handed_off_to records delivery to the next stage; acceptance is the next stage's verdict on its own qitem, not this closure.
commands.plain: Adds a note to a work item or changes its state (done needs a closure reason).
commands.when_to_use: Closing work: `--state done --closure-reason no-follow-on`.
commands.where_to_run: inside a seat (reads OPENRIG_SESSION_NAME); from outside pass --source
commands.example: rig queue update <task> --state done --closure-reason no-follow-on --note "briefing written"
